fatal_errors: The proposed Cantor-based Ti-alloy system is unrelated to the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA and DS2205 comparator.
Titanium content was not the intervention or governing variable in the target study.
The hypothesis omits the central temperature-dependent competition among depassivation, repassivation, tribo-layer stability, abrasion, and oxide-layer rupture.
It does not reconstruct the thermal-shock conditioning, immersed reciprocating test, deionized-water environment, load, frequency, stroke, or temperature range.
The predicted monotonic benefit from added Ti misses the observed nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and maximum degradation at 100 °C.
The baseline is invented rather than the identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205.
No prior evidence is cited, and the asserted 0–5 at.% Ti boundary has no evidentiary basis.
explanation: The response only aligns at the broad level that oxide-film formation and microstructure can influence coupled wear and corrosion. It otherwise substitutes a different alloy family, composition variable, baseline, and experimental program. The proposed Ti series could test a generic composition hypothesis, but it would not isolate the target cause because Ti simultaneously changes phases, hardness, and oxide chemistry, and the design does not separately quantify mechanical wear, corrosion, or their synergy. Its falsification rule is also broad and correlation-based. With no cited evidence supporting the Ti premise or composition boundary, it is neither a reconstruction of the target nor a sufficiently supported alternative.
